# Gas exchange and capnography

[All modules](README.md) · [Known misses](../validation/known-misses.md#gas-exchange) · 6 source files, 674 lines · 9 test files

## Purpose

<!-- hand:purpose -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

This module computes the patient's oxygen and carbon dioxide truth and the capnogram: an alveolar O2 store with
capillary equilibrium, shunt mixing and a mixed-venous buffer, a two-compartment CO2 store, the circulatory delay to
the oximeter probe, and the airway CO2 waveform of each breath with its pattern library and sampler. A
clinician-educator reads it to see how ventilation, cardiac output and apnoea move SpO2, PaCO2 and EtCO2; an embedding
developer reads it for the gas truths and the capnogram the monitor draws.
<!-- /hand:purpose -->

## Equations in words

<!-- hand:equations -->
> Draft — owner review pending.

- Oxygen is held as an alveolar store (FRC times the alveolar O2 fraction) in equilibrium with the pulmonary
  capillaries, mixed with shunt at mixed-venous content, and buffered by a mixed-venous blood pool with
  V_v·dCv/dt = Q·(Ca − Cv) − VO2; in apnoea with a patent airway, mass flow draws airway gas in (brief §4.3;
  research 03 §3.5; `l2/gas/o2.ts`).
- O2 saturation and content come from the blood model's dissociation curve, content
  13.4·Hb·S·(1 − COHb − MetHb) + 0.03·PO2 mL/L (`l2/gas/o2.ts`, `l2/blood/odc.ts`).
- CO2 is a two-compartment store, a fast compartment (lung gas, blood and well-perfused tissue) equal to PaCO2 and a
  slow muscle compartment, fitted to the apnoea rise of about 12 mmHg in the first minute then 3.4 mmHg/min (brief
  §4.4; research 03 §4.4; `l2/gas/co2.ts`, `l2/gas/params.ts`); at steady state PaCO2 = 0.863·VCO2/VA
  (research 03 §4.4; `l2/gas/params.ts`).
- Alveolar CO2 elimination is limited by pulmonary blood flow, so CO2 accumulates in an arrest and washes out at
  return of circulation; when flow falls, EtCO2 follows the washout of the alveolar gas with τ = V_alv/VA (research 03
  §4.4; `l2/gas/co2.ts`, `l2/gas/params.ts`).
- End-tidal PCO2 is PaCO2 times the lung module's end-tidal ratio, with a normal Pa − EtCO2 gradient of 2–5 mmHg
  (brief §4.4; `l2/gas/co2.ts`, `l2/gas/params.ts`).
- Pulmonary blood flow for gas exchange is the cardiac-output ratio × 0.075 L/min/kg × effective weight
  (`l2/gas/params.ts`); mean airway pressure raises the effective right-atrial pressure by 0.4 of its change (brief
  §4.9; `l2/gas/coupling.ts`).
- The saturation reaches the probe after a dead time of 15 s at the finger and 5 s at the ear at normal output,
  lengthened by low cardiac output and vasoconstriction up to 60 s (brief §4.3; research 03 §3.6; `l2/gas/delay.ts`).
- The capnogram of each breath is built from phases: an inspiratory downstroke, dead-space gas, an exponential
  phase II upswing and a sloped phase III plateau ending exactly at the breath's EtCO2, plus named patterns; the
  sampler is a transport delay and a first-order rise (brief §4.4; research 03 §4.1–§4.3; `l2/co2/capno.ts`).
<!-- /hand:equations -->
